3-95. Huy, Madison, and Ramona are working on the following problem and each begins her work differently.
1 3/8 ÷ 3/4

RAMONA:
There is one 3/4 in 1 3/8 and 5/8 left over. Then since 3/4 equals 6/8, those 5/8 are really 5/6 of one group. That means the answer is 1 5/6, that is, 3/4 divides 1 3/8 into 1 5/6 pieces of lengths 3/4.

MADISON:
Since 1 3/8 is the same as 11/8 and 3/4 is the same as 6/8, this problem is really the same as 11/8 ÷ 6/8. I can think of this as dividing 11 pieces into groups of 6 or 11 ÷ 6 = 11/6 = 1 5/6.

HUY:
Since a fraction is division, I can write a super fraction and use a Super Giant One to make an equivalent fraction with a denominator of one. Then I just simplify.
1 3/8 ÷ 3/4 = (1 3/8)/(3/4) = (11/8)/(3/4) · (4/3)/(4/3) = (44/24)/1 = 44/24 = 1 20/24 = 1 5/6.

Work with your team to make sense of each student’s approach to the problem. Then use each of the three approaches to do the following two problems.
a. 4/5 ÷ 1/2
b. 2 1/2 ÷ 3/4
